static_traits.name: Lin Jie
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with colleagues tending toward tension due to negative views of the career; has a group of supportive friends, but has not yet discussed these specific feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no past psychological problems or treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, strong logic, high cooperation (positive attitude)

basic_info.main_problem: Because I wanted to be an Architect as a child but became a Wedding planner, I feel my whole life has been ruined; this belief causes disappointment and a sense of failure.
basic_info.core_demands: These disappointments and feelings of failure are affecting overall well-being and job satisfaction and leading to career burnout; I hope through counseling to relieve these feelings and change how I view career and achievements, thereby obtaining more sustained satisfaction.
growth_experiences: Always longed to become an Architect since childhood; about 5 years ago after starting wedding-planning Work, gradually developed strong feelings of loss and failure due to the mismatch between ideals and reality, especially noticeable during busy or high-pressure projects.

core_beliefs: I am a failure / I have wasted my potential
Unless I realize my childhood ideal (becoming an Architect), I have no value

special_situations.event: Needing to collaborate with Architects on large wedding projects (e.g. interfacing with an Architect on venue layout last month)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not become an Architect, it means I made the wrong life choice and am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Being Distracted at Work, becoming cold toward colleagues or Withdrawing, avoiding directly facing loss and jealousy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I were an Architect, my life would be much better; I have ruined my own life

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only becoming an Architect counts as success; otherwise it is total failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing with the ideal career and being harsh on oneself, leading to Decreased drive
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Either become an Architect or be a failure

special_situations.event: When a wedding goes smoothly and clients are highly satisfied
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Achievements unrelated to the childhood ideal do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, dismissing satisfaction as 'fleeting, unimportant'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These successes are not real achievements

special_situations.event: After contact with Architects or when Reflecting on career choices alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I have already missed the only opportunity; there is no changing it now
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Gives up exploring or trying to change, falls into regret and self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is already too late; I cannot change anything

core_conflict.wish: Longs to realize the self-ideal and gain a recognized sense of achievement and worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that acknowledging the real choice means 'failure' and worthlessness, worrying about losing the sense of control over life
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of certainty and control through black-and-white self-evaluation
Avoids exposing vulnerability and jealousy by withdrawing from colleagues and self-blaming
Belittles current achievements to avoid facing the sadness of the ideal falling through

object_relations.self_representation: Sees oneself as wasting potential, a failure
object_relations.object_representation: Imagining Architects/others as superior people who judge one's worth

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited in counseling to review success cases or client praise
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these successes 'do not count' and cannot prove one's worth
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying positive experiences, using expressions like 'just good luck / not a real achievement', with a calm but firm tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing topics such as 'whether there are still choices / whether the only chance was missed'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding acknowledging reality as total failure, suppressing sadness and helplessness with rational analysis
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in objective, analytical language, avoids the emotional level, restrained tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When feeling shame and resentment from comparing with high achievers (e.g. Architects)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning outward-directed aggression and dissatisfaction toward oneself, deepening the self-perception of 'I am worthless'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming expressions (e.g. 'It is all my fault'), low tone, reducing interaction with others.

manifestations: Feeling overall unsatisfied and unfulfilled in wedding-planning Work
Even after completing a perfect wedding and receiving high client recognition, the sense of satisfaction is quickly belittled as fleeting
outcomes: Persistent disappointment and sense of failure

manifestations: Believing one has missed the only choice, feeling 'unable to change'
Reinforced sense of being trapped by existing choices during high-pressure periods

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Internalizing 'only becoming an Architect counts as success' as an absolute standard
In sessions, tends to define self-worth by a single career ideal

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism (such as 'I wasted my potential' and 'I made the wrong life choices')
Repeatedly scrutinizing and negating one's achievements in the narrative

exception_events.target_problem: In large or high-pressure wedding projects, the client usually views not having become an Architect as failure, thus feeling loss, Decreased drive, and becoming cold or Withdrawing in interactions with colleagues.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In several 'very beautiful' weddings, everything went smoothly and clients were extremely satisfied; at the time the client gained joy and satisfaction, and was not swallowed by the sense of failure as usual.
exception_events.reason: Different support: positive feedback from clients and the visible success of smooth weddings shifted attention from comparison to present results, briefly reducing catastrophizing and comparison.

positive_force: Has a supportive network of friends (although this topic has not yet been discussed with them)
In multiple projects created high-quality results and gained high client satisfaction
Willing to seek help and actively accept new strategies (good collaborative attitude)
Has tried mindfulness and thought recording, with some self-help skill foundation
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking are prominent
Excessive comparison and negating positive experiences, maintaining the 'failure' self-schema
Negative predictions about the future (believing the only opportunity has been missed)
High work pressure amplifying negative emotions and thoughts
Tense relationships with colleagues, forming a negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing and self-belittling automatic thoughts (such as 'my life is ruined' and 'I wasted my potential')
antecedent: When in contact with or seeing Architects
target_behavior.core_reason: The mismatch between the childhood ideal (Architect) and the real career internalized as a rigid success standard, leading to persistent comparison and Self-denial
target_behavior.function: Briefly avoiding facing loss and uncertainty, maintaining a sense of control through self-blame
target_behavior.consequence: Well-being and Decline in job satisfaction, worsening Occupational burnout

target_behavior.behavior: Becomes curt / cold toward colleagues or withdraws
antecedent: When the sense of self-failure is strong
target_behavior.core_reason: Turning inner frustration and resentment against the self and relationships to avoid exposing vulnerability and being judged
target_behavior.function: Briefly relieves shame and jealousy, escapes evaluated situations
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with colleagues, further weakening Social support and Work engagement
